chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Hashim al-Bajali, from Salim Abu Khadija, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
A person asked him while I was present, so he said: 'Sometimes I enter the mosque and some of our companions are praying the Asr and some of them are praying the Zuhr.'
So he (peace be upon him) said: 'I ordered them with this. If they had prayed at one (same) time, they would have been recognised, and they would have been seized by their necks.'

key_terms.الظُّهْر: Zuhr — the midday prayer, obligatory, performed after the sun passes its zenith
key_terms.الْعَصْر: Asr — the afternoon prayer, obligatory, performed in the mid-afternoon
key_terms.بِرِقَابِهِمْ: by their necks — an Arabic idiom for violent arrest or execution

ai.seo_question: Why did Imam al-Sadiq order his companions to pray Zuhr and Asr at different times?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) explains that he deliberately instructed his Shia companions to pray the Zuhr and Asr prayers at different times. This was a taqiyya (precautionary dissimulation) measure: praying in unison as a distinct group would have made them identifiable to the Abbasid authorities who persecuted the Shia, potentially leading to their arrest. The phrase 'seized by their necks' was a well-understood idiom for execution or violent arrest in the early Islamic period.
